entries.def:
μῶμος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX, of physical blemishes : Lev.21.17 ff., Deu.15.21, Sng.4.7, al. (מאוּם); of mental defect, Sir.20.24, al. ;] 
__1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace. 
__2. In LXX, perb. because of resemblance to a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, 1Pe.1.19, and see Hort., in l); metaphorically, of licentious persons, 2Pe.2.13.†
(AS)

μωραίνω
(μωρός), [in LXX: Isa.19.11, Jer.10.14; 51.17 (בָּעַר ni.), 2Ki.24.10, Isa.44.25 R (שָׂכַל ni., pi.)* ;] 
__1. cl., to be foolish, play the fool. 
__2. LXX and NT, causal, to make foolish: 1Co.1.20 pass., to become foolish: Rom.1.22 of salt that has lost its flavour, become tasteless: Mat.5.13, Luk.14.34.†
(AS)

μωρός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX for נָבָל, etc.; frequently in Sir. ;] 
__1. prop., of the nerves, dull, sluggish (Hipp., Arist.). 
__2. Of the mind, dull, stupid, foolish: Mat.5.22 (see Field, Notes, 3 ff.) Mat.7.26; 23.17, 19 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) Mat.25.2-3, 8, 1Co.3.18; 4.10; of things, παράδοσις, Mrk.7.13 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) : ζητήσεις, 2Ti.2.23, Tit.3.9; τὸ μ. τ. θεοῦ, 1Co.1.25 τὰ μ. τ. κόσμου, 1Co.1.27.†
(AS)

Μωυσῆς (Μωϋσῆς, T; Μωσῆς, Rec.), -έως, dative - (as LXX: Exo.5.20, al.), and -εῖ, accusative -ῆν (ac LXX) and -έα (Luk.16.29 only) (Heb. מֹשֶׁה), 
Moses: Mat.8.4; 17.3-4, al.; νόμος Μωυσέως, Luk.2.22; 24.44, Jhn.7.23, Act.13.39; 15.5; 28.23, 1Co.9.9, Heb.10.28; by meton., of the books of Moses, Luk.16.29; 24.27, Act.15.21, 2Co.3.15 
(AS)

Ναασσών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחְשׁוֹן), 
Naasson: Mat.1.4, Luk.3.32.†
(AS)

Ναζαρά
(Mat.4.13­ L, -άθ­Luk.4.16) 
Ναζαρέθ (Mat.21.11, Act.10.38), 
Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, 
indecl. (Semitic form uncertain), 
Nazareth: Mat.2.23, Mrk.1.9, Luk.1.26; 2.4, 39; 2.51, Jhn.1.45-46.†
(AS)

Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(on the Semitic form, see Dalman, Gr., 141 n.) 
a Nazarene: Mrk.1.24; 10.47; 14.67; 16.6, Luk.4.34; 24.19.†
(AS)
